QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_37

question.text: At what level of collateral utilization does the exchange cancel all unexecuted orders of a clearing member?

explanation.text: The Logic: When a clearing member's collateral utilization reaches 90%, the exchange automatically cancels all their unexecuted (pending) orders. This is a risk containment measure to prevent further exposure buildup. The Trap: 80% may trigger a warning but not order cancellation. 95% and 100% are too late for this initial action. The 90% trigger is designed to provide a safety buffer before complete depletion. Cross-Exam Context: The 90% threshold is consistent across all exchange-traded derivative segments. Series VIII also tests this threshold for equity derivatives. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Smart risk management involves setting internal thresholds at 70-80% to trigger margin top-up actions well before the exchange's 90% cancellation trigger.
